title: Nala — 5yo Cocker Spaniel: lethargy, icterus & dark urine
presentation: 5-year-old female neutered Cocker Spaniel, three days of lethargy and inappetence. The owner thought her gums looked yellow this morning, and her urine is the colour of strong tea.

stages.title: Read the first-line bloods
stages.briefing: On presentation: HR 140 bpm, RR 36/min, temperature 39.1°C. Mucous membranes pale and icteric, CRT 2 seconds. New grade II/VI systolic murmur. No external haemorrhage, no access to rodenticide, onions or zinc, no medication. In-house PCV 14% (ref 37–55), total solids 7.4 g/dL (ref 5.4–7.5).
stages.prompt: Which findings tell you the red cells are being destroyed rather than lost?

options.label: PCV 14% with total solids 7.4 g/dL
options.detail: Anaemia with no fall in protein

options.label: Icteric mucous membranes
options.detail: Bilirubin from red cell breakdown

options.label: Tea-coloured urine
options.detail: Haemoglobinuria and bilirubinuria

options.label: Grade II/VI systolic murmur
options.detail: A flow murmur — consequence, not cause

options.label: Temperature 39.1°C
options.detail: Fits inflammation of any origin

stages.explanation: Haemorrhage takes protein with it. A PCV of 14% alongside normal total solids is the single most useful line on this panel: the cells are going somewhere other than out of a vessel, and the icterus and pigmenturia say where. The murmur is a flow murmur that resolves as the PCV rises — chasing it as primary heart disease is the classic wrong turn — and a mild fever fits immune-mediated inflammation and sepsis equally well.

stages.title: Confirm haemolysis before treating
stages.briefing: You have IV access, and pre-treatment samples are in hand. Immunosuppression is the likely next step, so anything infectious has to be excluded first.
stages.prompt: Which tests do you run before the first dose of glucocorticoid?

options.label: Blood smear for spherocytes and agglutination
options.detail: Fastest evidence of immune destruction

options.label: Saline agglutination test
options.detail: Separates true agglutination from rouleaux

options.label: Reticulocyte count
options.detail: Regenerative or not changes the prognosis

options.label: Biochemistry with total and direct bilirubin
options.detail: Grades the icterus, screens the liver

options.label: Vector-borne panel — Babesia, Mycoplasma haemocanis, Ehrlichia
options.detail: Infectious triggers must be excluded before steroids

options.label: Direct Coombs test as the first-line test
options.detail: Slower and less specific than a smear; it does not decide the next hour

options.label: Bile acid stimulation test
options.detail: Not while the icterus has an obvious pre-hepatic cause

stages.explanation: A smear read by someone who knows what a spherocyte looks like is the highest-yield test in the building, and the saline dilution stops rouleaux masquerading as agglutination. Reticulocytes and bilirubin quantify what the smear shows. The infectious panel is not academic: immunosuppressing a babesiosis is a way to lose a patient. Coombs and bile acids are not wrong tests in general — they are the wrong tests to wait on now.

stages.title: Narrow the cause of the haemolysis
stages.briefing: Smear: marked spherocytosis with autoagglutination that persists after 1:4 saline dilution. Reticulocytes 210 ×10⁹/L (regenerative). Total bilirubin 68 µmol/L (ref <10). Platelets 165 ×10⁹/L. Babesia and M. haemocanis PCR negative, no travel outside the UK. Abdominal ultrasound: mild splenomegaly, no mass, no free fluid. Thoracic radiographs unremarkable.

options.label: Primary immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia
options.detail: Spherocytes plus true agglutination, no trigger found

options.label: Secondary IMHA from an occult neoplasm
options.detail: Imaging lowers the odds but does not exclude it

options.label: Zinc or onion toxicosis
options.detail: No access, and neither gives true agglutination

options.label: Babesiosis
options.detail: PCR negative with no travel history

options.label: Haemorrhage into a body cavity
options.detail: Total solids normal, both cavities dry

stages.explanation: True agglutination surviving saline dilution, with spherocytes and a regenerative response, is immune-mediated destruction. Whether it is primary or secondary is not settled by one clear ultrasound, which is why an occult neoplasm stays on the list and is looked for again later. The toxicoses produce Heinz bodies or eccentrocytes, not spherocytes, and the normal protein rules the bleed out on the first panel.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Saline agglutination positive, spherocytosis marked, infectious panel negative, no mass on imaging, no drug or toxin exposure.

options.label: Primary immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia
options.detail: Immune destruction with no identifiable trigger

options.label: Anaemia of chronic kidney disease
options.detail: Non-regenerative, and no azotaemia here

options.label: Blood loss anaemia from an undetected bleed
options.detail: Protein would have fallen with the cells

options.label: Zinc toxicosis
options.detail: Needs a metal foreign body and gives a different smear

options.label: Primary hepatobiliary disease
options.detail: Would not produce spherocytes or agglutination

stages.explanation: Primary IMHA is a diagnosis of exclusion built on positive evidence: spherocytes and true agglutination for the mechanism, a negative infectious and toxin search for the trigger. Naming it commits you to immunosuppression plus thromboprophylaxis, and to repeating the hunt for an underlying cause if the response is poor.
